payload.description: Connection details for the source, passed as a flat set of keys. Either include `credential_id` (an id from data-warehouse-stored-credentials-list, for the same source_type) to use credentials a user already stored — the stored secrets are used server-side and are never returned, and the credential stays available for data-warehouse-source-setup — or pass the credential fields inline. Inline keys depend on source_type. For database sources: host, port, database, user, password, schema. For SaaS sources: api_key or OAuth fields. For source_type "Custom" (a user-defined REST API): `manifest_json` (a stringified RESTAPIConfig describing client.base_url, auth, and resources) plus `auth_token` (bearer), `auth_api_key` (api_key), or `auth_password` (http_basic). Use external-data-sources-wizard (pass source_type) to see required fields per source type. Do not pass unresolved {"secretRef": ...} objects. Example with a stored credential: {"credential_id": "<id>"}.

source_type.description: Required. The source type name (e.g. "Postgres", "MySQL", "Stripe"). Use external-data-sources-wizard to list the valid source types and their required fields.
